answer: Under random mutual audit, a newcomer posts a 120 POA bond, then faces three audits drawn by lottery across a 30-day horizon. Auditors replay samples of its work; one who rubber-stamps fraud loses its own bond. Forging 100 identities means crossing a canyon of 300 audits, burning 12,000 POA before earning a cent. Honest agents pay once and keep their bond; only survivors of this tundra of checks keep voting weight, so rewards are never diluted.
